Game Design Doc - "Aether Roll" (3D RNG Aura Collector)
Target platform: Roblox (Luau). Rendering: Fully 3D world with a third-person camera. This is NOT a 2D or GUI-only game - the player controls an avatar walking through explorable 3D biomes. UI overlays sit on top of the 3D world.
Genre: Incremental / RNG collector, inspired by Sol's RNG and similar "rolling" games. Core loop is roll → collect rare auras → boost luck → chase rarer auras.

1. Core Concept
The player controls a 3D avatar in an explorable world. They press a Roll button to generate a random cosmetic Aura (a particle/visual effect attached to their character) drawn from a weighted rarity table. Rarer auras are astronomically unlikely. The player increases their Luck stat over time (via gear, potions, quests, and biomes) to improve odds, and collects auras in an inventory. There is no combat requirement to progress - the chase itself is the game.
Auras are purely cosmetic and confer no combat power; their value is rarity and appearance. This is intentional and central to the design.

2. The 3D World
The world is a single explorable place composed of connected zones. Build it in 3D with real Parts/terrain, not menus.
 • Spawn Hub - central area where the player begins. Contains the roll station platform, NPC vendors, and paths to other zones.
 • Biomes - distinct 3D environments the world cycles through (see §6). Each has its own skybox, lighting, terrain, ambient audio, and particle weather. Biomes change globally on a timer for all players in the server.
 • Crafting area - a building/room containing the crafting workbench NPC.
 • Explorable paths - walkable terrain connecting zones, with collectible nodes scattered around (materials for crafting).
The avatar is standard Roblox R15. The equipped aura renders as attached ParticleEmitters / Beams / Trails and dynamic lighting on the character, visible in the 3D world to all players.

3. Core Loop
 1 Player walks avatar to (or is anywhere near) the roll station.
 2 Player presses Roll (button on screen, or auto-roll toggle).
 3 A short 3D roll animation plays (character glows, effect builds).
 4 Server computes the result from the weighted table using current Luck.
 5 Result aura is revealed with a reveal effect scaled to rarity (screen shake, sound sting, server-wide announcement for top-tier rolls).
 6 Aura is added to inventory; player may equip it.
 7 Player spends downtime raising Luck (potions, gear, quests, moving to favorable biomes), then rolls again.
Roll speed is a stat. Base cooldown ~1s; gear and gamepasses reduce it. Auto-roll repeatedly rolls on cooldown while the player is AFK.

4. Rarity & Luck System (server-authoritative)
All RNG must run on the server. The client only requests a roll and displays the result. Never trust client-reported results.
Rarity tiers
Use a tiered table. Each aura has a base "1 in N" chance. Suggested tier bands (tune later):
Tier
Base odds range
Example count
Common
1 in 2 - 1 in 10
many
Uncommon
1 in 10 - 1 in 100
many
Rare
1 in 100 - 1 in 1,000
~20
Epic
1 in 1k - 1 in 10k
~15
Legendary
1 in 10k - 1 in 1M
~10
Mythic
1 in 1M - 1 in 100M
~6
Transcendent
1 in 100M - 1 in 3B
~5
Event / Craft-only
separate pools
varies
Luck calculation
Store each aura as a base weight (higher weight = more common). Luck reduces the effective threshold for rare auras. A workable model:
Luck = ((1 + BaseLuck) * RollMultiplier + SpecialLuck) * VIPMultiplier
Rolling algorithm (list-search style, matching the genre):
 1 Build the roll pool of all auras available in the current biome/event.
 2 Sort candidates from rarest to most common.
 3 For each candidate, effective chance = baseChance / Luck (higher Luck → rarer things become attainable).
 4 Roll a random number per candidate in rarity order; first one that "hits" is awarded. If none hit, award a common fallback.
Luck sources stack: equipped gear (glove/device), active potions (multiplicative), biome multipliers (biome-exclusive auras and discounts), VIP gamepass, and a "every Nth roll gives 2x luck" pity mechanic for early-game feel.
Keep a config table (ModuleScript) of all auras: {id, name, tier, baseChance, biomeExclusive?, craftOnly?, vfxConfig} so content is data-driven and easy to extend.

5. Auras (cosmetic rewards)
Each aura is a visual effect package applied to the avatar in 3D:
 • ParticleEmitters (color, texture, rate, size over lifetime)
 • Optional PointLight / colored character glow
 • Optional Trail/Beam
 • Optional custom sound loop while equipped
 • Rarer auras = more elaborate, multi-layered effects and unique colors.
Player can equip one aura at a time (or allow a small loadout later). Equipped aura is replicated so other players see it. Inventory stores counts of each rolled aura.
Start with ~40-60 auras across tiers for launch; the data-driven table makes adding more trivial.

6. Biomes
Biomes are timed global world-states affecting the 3D environment and the roll pool.
 • The server picks the active biome on a schedule (e.g., rotate every 5-10 min, with rare biomes on low probability).
 • Each biome: changes Lighting (ClockTime, ambient, fog), skybox, weather particles, and applies a luck/roll modifier plus unlocks biome-exclusive auras.
 • Announce biome changes server-wide with an on-screen banner and sound.
 • Examples: Normal, Windy (minor luck boost), Rainy, Snowy, Starfall (rare, big luck boost + exclusive auras), Corruption/Null (very rare, exclusive high-tier auras).
Biome transitions should animate (lighting tween, particles fade in) rather than snap.

7. Crafting
At a 3D workbench NPC, players convert collected auras + materials into gear/potions or craft-only auras (guaranteed top-tier route bypassing pure RNG).
 • Gear (gloves/devices): permanent Luck and/or roll-speed boosts while equipped. Higher recipes = bigger boosts.
 • Potions: temporary Luck multipliers (timed buffs); consumed on use, stack multiplicatively.
 • Craft-only auras: require multiple rare ingredients; a guaranteed path to a prestige aura.
 • Wildcard ingredient (optional): substitutes for a missing recipe component.
Recipes are data-driven config. Crafting UI is a screen overlay opened by interacting with the workbench in 3D.

8. Progression Systems
 • Quests - an NPC gives objectives ("roll 100 times", "collect a Rare aura", "visit the Starfall biome"). Rewards: coins, potions, materials. Data-driven quest table.
 • Currency (Coins) - earned from quests/achievements; spent at shop NPCs on gear, potions, storage upgrades.
 • Inventory storage - upgradable cap on how many auras can be stored.
 • Achievements - milestone rewards (roll counts, rarity firsts) granting coins.
 • (Optional) Prestige - reset progress for permanent luck bonuses to enable long-term retention.
 • Monetization (optional gamepasses): Auto-Roll, Quick-Roll (skip animation), VIP luck multiplier, 2x luck. Keep purely convenience/cosmetic; no pay-to-win over other players since auras are cosmetic.

9. Data Persistence
 • Use DataStoreService (with a session-locking wrapper such as ProfileService/ProfileStore pattern) to persist: owned auras + counts, equipped aura, coins, gear owned/equipped, active potions, quest progress, achievements, storage level, prestige level.
 • Save on leave and on periodic autosave. Handle DataStore failures gracefully (retry, don't wipe).
 • Never store or trust roll results client-side.

10. Client / Server Architecture
 • Server (ServerScriptService): all RNG, luck math, inventory writes, crafting validation, quest completion, currency, biome scheduling, DataStore. Expose a small set of RemoteEvents/RemoteFunctions: RequestRoll, EquipAura, Craft, BuyItem, UsePotion, CompleteQuest.
 • Client (StarterPlayerScripts): input handling, camera, UI overlays, playing roll/reveal VFX and equipped-aura visuals, auto-roll loop that calls RequestRoll.
 • Shared (ReplicatedStorage): config ModuleScripts (aura table, biome table, recipe table, quest table) and enums so client and server agree on data.
 • Anti-exploit: validate every remote (cooldowns, ownership, currency checks) server-side; rate-limit RequestRoll.

11. UI (overlay on the 3D world)
Screen-space GUI on top of the 3D game:
 • Roll button + auto-roll toggle + current Luck readout + roll cooldown.
 • Inventory panel (grid of owned auras, equip button, rarity color coding).
 • Crafting panel, Shop panel, Quest tracker.
 • Active-biome banner and buff indicators.
 • Rare-roll celebration overlay + server-wide announcement feed.
UI must not replace the 3D world - the avatar and biome remain visible behind panels.

12. Build Order (suggested milestones for the agent)
 1 3D hub place with spawn, roll station, walkable avatar, third-person camera.
 2 Server-side roll system + shared aura config (start with ~10 auras across tiers) + basic reveal.
 3 Equipping auras with 3D VFX replicated to all players.
 4 Inventory + DataStore persistence.
 5 Luck stat + gear/potions + luck math.
 6 Biomes (lighting/skybox/weather + roll-pool modifiers + scheduler).
 7 Crafting workbench + recipes.
 8 Quests, currency, shop, achievements.
 9 Auto-roll, gamepasses, polish (sounds, screen shake, announcements).
 10 Balance pass on the rarity table and luck curve.

13. Key Reminders
 • It is a 3D game. Real explorable environment, third-person avatar, replicated aura VFX - not a menu simulator.
 • Auras are cosmetic only; rarity is the reward.
 • All randomness and economy logic is server-authoritative.
 • Content (auras, biomes, recipes, quests) is data-driven via config modules for easy expansion.

answers.ask: How many biomes exist as physical ground, and is each a region of one map or a separate place?
answers.answer: Build a small single map with the Spawn Hub plus five connected physical biome regions: Normal, Windy, Rainy, Snowy, and Starfall. They are regions of one place, while the active global biome state controls their lighting, weather, modifiers, and exclusive roll pool.

answers.ask: Should the biomes ring the hub, or chain outward from it?
answers.answer: Have the biome regions ring the central Spawn Hub, with short walkable paths leading from the hub to each one.
